## Jon Loomer — Campaign volume, AI disclosures, and when to simplify

_From: `[email]` · 2026-06-20T06:30:08+00:00_

96 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 This week’s Loop covers campaign volume, the new AI disclosure checkbox, why best practices won’t guarantee results, country segmentation, and a common mistake with restrictions. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Hey, Mark. This week’s Loop covers campaign volume, the new AI disclosure checkbox, why best practices won’t guarantee results, country segmentation, and a common mistake with restrictions. 
 Here’s what you need to know from the past week... 
 1. GET HELP NAVIGATING WHAT CHANGED 
 Power Hitters Club - Elite is the best way to get direct access to me while also connecting with a community of advertisers who are working through the same challenges you are. You get weekly strategy sessions, weekly webinars, a private group, an ad briefs library, access to JonBot, and a discount on one-on-ones. Save 30% off any membership level for a limited time. 
 [LEARN MORE] 
 2. HOW MANY CAMPAIGNS SHOULD YOU RUN AT ONCE? 
 While there isn't a universal threshold for the number of campaigns you should use, I wanted to put together an exercise that compiles the questions you should ask to help determine the right number of campaigns for you. It's focused on budget, primary goal, secondary goals, costs, business requirements, and more. 
 [READ NOW] 
 3. HAVE YOU SEEN THE NEW AI DISCLOSURE CHECKBOX? 
 Legislation is popping up that requires disclosures when you use AI to create or alter images and videos. That's relevant if you've noticed the latest AI disclosure checkbox in Ads Manager. Another big item this week is that the default conversion attribution setting for ChatGPT ads appears to be 30-day click and view. Can that possibly be right? 
 [READ NOW] 
 4. BEST PRACTICES WON'T GUARANTEE RESULTS 
 You're prioritizing a simplified approach to campaign construction with minimal campaigns and ad sets, consolidating your budget toward a conversion goal. Assuming this will guarantee results is no different than assuming a complicated strategy will. It's the focus of this week's Pubcast Shot (7 minutes). 
 [LISTEN NOW] 
 5. SHOULD YOU SEPARATE COUNTRIES IN SALES CAMPAIGNS? 
 I responded to a question this week that started rather simple, but it got more complicated quickly. Should you create separate ad sets for similarly priced countries by CPM when running a sales campaign using worldwide targeting? Should you use worldwide targeting at all? There was a lot to discuss. It's the focus of this week's Pubcast Question (4 minutes). 
 [LISTEN NOW] 
 6. YOU DON'T NEED TO DO THAT 
 The restrictions most advertisers make are rarely necessary, especially when optimizing for a purchase. You assume you'll get better results by removing less valuable placements and demographics. But the only times those restrictions might be necessary, value rules present a better solution. 
 [WATCH NOW] 
 I hope you found this recap useful. If you have any questions, don't hesitate to ask. Have a great weekend! 
 Cheers, 
 Jon
